sections.h2: What should you know before selling a house in Avon, Ohio?
sections.html:
Avon is a Lorain County suburb in the Cleveland area where most homes are owner-occupied and about two in five households include children. The city covers 20.79 square miles of land, which makes it nearly twice the size of neighboring Avon Lake, and the Census Bureau estimated its 2025 population at 25,611.

The land was part of Township Number 7 in the Western Reserve, which received its first permanent settlers in 1814. The township was organized in 1818 under the name Xeuma, later called Troy Township, and renamed Avon Township when Lorain County formed in 1824. An Avon post office opened in 1825, the area was incorporated as a village in 1917, and it became the City of Avon in 1961.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Avon homes?
sections.html:
Home values run high in Avon. QuickFacts lists the 2020 to 2024 owner-occupied rate at 88.3% and the median owner-occupied home value at $395,900. It shows 9,502 households with 2.63 people each, a median gross rent of $1,796, and median monthly owner costs of $2,471 with a mortgage and $818 without.

  • At the 2020 census, 41.5% of Avon households included children under 18.
  • Married-couple households made up 64.2% of all households, and the median age was 40.7.
  • The city counted 9,208 housing units in 2020, with 4.2% vacant.

Those numbers describe a market where buyers expect move-in condition. A seller who cannot take on repairs, or who is dealing with a divorce, a relocation or an estate, may find a direct purchase simpler than preparing the house for the open market.

sections.h2: Where do Avon property tax dollars go?
sections.html:
Most of an Avon tax bill funds the schools. The City of Avon's welcome packet breaks down the 2025 tax year as shown below, and the city itself receives 10.12% of the total.

How the 2025 Avon property tax bill was divided, per the city's welcome packet
RecipientShare of the bill
Avon Schools66.43%
Lorain County19.18%
City of Avon10.12%
Lorain JVSD3.63%
Lorain Health0.64%

The same packet says Avon collects a municipal income tax at 1.95%, with a credit of up to 1.7% for residents who work in another city, administered through the Regional Income Tax Agency. A buyer comparing Avon with a nearby town will look at both numbers.

Ask the Lorain County Treasurer for the due dates in your closing year. The treasurer listed February 13, 2026 for the first half and July 31, 2026 for the second half, after the second date moved because of the House Bill 186 inflation cap credit. The treasurer also runs an optional monthly escrow payment program, and title and mortgage companies that print their own bills avoid duplicate bill fees.

sections.h2: Which Avon schools and amenities do buyers ask about?
sections.html:
Avon Local School District serves the city. Its buildings are the Early Learning Center for preschool and kindergarten, Avon East Elementary for grades 1 and 2, Heritage Elementary for grades 3 through 5, Avon Middle School for grades 6 through 8 and Avon High School for grades 9 through 12. Avon Middle School was named a Blue Ribbon school for 2020 by the U.S. Department of Education. Private options listed by the city include Holy Trinity School, St. Mary School and Avon Montessori Academy.

The library is a branch of the Lorain Public Library, and a 16,000 square foot expansion opened in January 2023. The city runs parks and facilities along Detroit Road and Schwartz Road, an aquatic facility, a senior center and a dog park, and the Lake Erie Crushers play on Baseball Boulevard. Municipal water and sewer, curbside trash on Mondays and fall leaf pickup are all city or contracted services, so a buyer can read what comes with the house before an offer. The Service Department clears snow on more than 250 lane miles of road in a priority order of main, secondary and then residential streets, and the city belongs to the Northeast Ohio Public Energy Council for gas and electric supply, which a buyer can stay with or leave.

sections.h2: What Avon rules affect a house you plan to sell?
sections.html:
The Avon Building Department and Zoning Department share City Hall at 36600 Detroit Road. The city tells residents to contact the Building Department for a pool, irrigation, deck, patio, shed, finished basement, fence, new roof, siding or any addition, and says contractors must be registered with the city. Check that any of those projects at your house have a closed permit.

  • Utilities: water and sewer bills are sent monthly with a due date of the 25th, and meters report actual daily use. Call the Utilities Department to stop service in your name after closing.
  • Sprinklers: an in-ground system needs an approved backflow device that is tested each year before June 30, with results sent to the city.
  • Short-term rentals: a 2021 ordinance extending a moratorium stated that the zoning code prohibits uses it does not list, and that short-term rentals are not listed. Ask the Zoning Department whether any rule has changed before you market the house to an investor.

Avon also keeps a Do Not Knock list, where an address stays registered for three years. A seller who is tired of unsolicited offers can ask the city about it.

sections.h2: How does the Ohio paperwork work for an Avon seller?
sections.html:
Ohio requires the seller of a one to four unit residence to complete the state property disclosure form and deliver it to the buyer, with exceptions that include estate fiduciary sales and transfers to relatives (ORC 5302.30). A buyer who gets the form after signing can cancel in writing within three business days.

The deed has to be signed by the owner and acknowledged by a notary or another official named in ORC 5301.01. It is recorded with the county recorder where the land sits, and ORC 5301.25 treats an unrecorded deed as fraudulent against a later purchaser who had no knowledge of it. Before recording, the deed goes through the Lorain County Auditor, which accepts conveyances only in person or by e-file, requires typed forms and returns anything incomplete. Lorain County staff cannot complete forms for you, so let the title company file them.

sections.h2: When is a cash sale the better choice in Avon?
sections.html:
A cash sale fits when you need a firm closing date more than a top price. In a high-value suburb, a listing can bring strong offers, but it also brings staging, showings and buyer repair requests.

Compare the net from each route. Add agent fees, repair costs, mortgage payments, taxes and utilities for the weeks a listing may take, then compare that total with a direct offer. Ask for the offer in writing with a closing date, and keep a copy of the signed disclosure form for your records.

faqs.q: Can I rent my Avon house short term before I sell?
faqs.a: Check with the Zoning Department first. A 2021 city ordinance said short-term rentals are not a listed use in the residential districts and are therefore prohibited, so ask whether the rule has changed.

faqs.q: Who processes the deed for an Avon sale?
faqs.a: The Lorain County Auditor processes the transfer, and the county recorder files the deed. The auditor takes conveyances in person or by e-file only, and a title company normally handles both steps.

faqs.q: What share of an Avon tax bill goes to the schools?
faqs.a: Avon Schools received 66.43% of the 2025 tax year bill according to the city's welcome packet. Lorain County received 19.18% and the city 10.12%.

faqs.q: Do I need to disclose problems when I sell in Avon?
faqs.a: Yes, on the Ohio property disclosure form for one to four unit homes. The form covers water, sewer, structure and known defects, and a buyer who gets it late can rescind within three business days.

faqs.q: Which permits should be closed before I sell in Avon?
faqs.a: Any permit for a deck, pool, shed, fence, roof, siding, finished basement or addition. Call the Building Department at City Hall to ask about open permits and unfinished inspections.
